summary: Adds a Flask search endpoint and a Stripe config file. It also changes items pagination, downgrades lodash, loosens the Dockerfile and deploy script, and echoes the PR title in CI.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: search_items puts the q request parameter straight into the SQL text with an f-string. A quote in q ends the string literal and lets the caller append arbitrary SQL.
findings.consequence: Any caller of /search can read every table in items.db. Depending on the driver, the caller may also change rows.
findings.fix: Use a ? placeholder in the query and pass q as a bound parameter.
findings.suggested_change: cur.execute("SELECT id, name, price FROM items WHERE name = ?", (q,))

findings.title: Pagination offset skips the first page
findings.problem: list_items now computes the offset as page * PAGE_SIZE. Page 1, the default, therefore starts at row 20 instead of row 0.
findings.consequence: Clients never see the first 20 items. Every page shows the rows that belong to the next page.

findings.title: Stripe key committed to source
findings.problem: config.py hardcodes what looks like a Stripe API key. The key is now in the repository history.
findings.consequence: Anyone with read access to the repository can make payment API calls as the shop.
findings.fix: Revoke and rotate the key. Read it from an environment variable or a secret store.

findings.title: PR title interpolated into a shell step
findings.problem: The workflow expands the pull request title directly into the run script. A title with a quote or $( ) runs as shell code on the runner.
findings.consequence: Any pull request author can run commands in CI. They can then tamper with the build or read its token.
findings.fix: Pass the title through an env variable and reference that variable in double quotes.

findings.title: lodash downgraded to a vulnerable release
findings.problem: The change moves lodash from 4.18.1 to 4.17.15. Version 4.17.15 has known command injection and prototype pollution flaws.
findings.consequence: Front-end code that uses lodash template, set or zipObjectDeep becomes exploitable again.
findings.fix: Keep lodash at 4.18.1 in both package.json and package-lock.json.

findings.title: Container now runs as root
findings.problem: The change removes the useradd step and the USER 10001 line. The Flask server now runs as root inside the container.
findings.consequence: Any code execution bug in the app, such as the new search injection path, gets root inside the container.
findings.fix: Restore the unprivileged app user and the USER 10001 instruction before CMD.

findings.title: Base image no longer pinned
findings.problem: The change replaces the pinned python:3.12.7-slim-bookworm image with python:latest. Each build may now pull a different Python major version.
findings.consequence: Builds can break or change behaviour without any change to the code. The full image is also much larger than slim.
findings.fix: Pin the base image to the previous explicit slim tag.

findings.title: Unquoted path in recursive delete
findings.problem: The script now passes DEPLOY_DIR to rm -rf without quotes. A path with a space splits into separate arguments.
findings.consequence: A deploy with such a path deletes the wrong directories on the server.
findings.fix: Quote the variable and keep the empty-value guard.

findings.title: Changed endpoints have no tests
findings.problem: The change adds the search endpoint and changes the list_items offset. The repository has no test files covering either.
findings.consequence: Regressions like the pagination offset bug reach users without being caught.
findings.fix: Add tests for /search and for the first page of /items.
